verdict:
VERDICT: sound but over-billed. Everything the route asserts as proved is proved -- I checked all seven proofs line by line and re-verified each claim independently in exact arithmetic (totals in /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-lane/TOTALS.txt: 410228 rise-bound checks, 48051 general peak checks, 9184 autonomy projections, 70000+ sharpened-peak checks, three families rebuilt from the text at seven sizes each, two exhaustive a=1 censuses). Nothing is circular, no oracle is assumed, no polynomial class is claimed, and the three families are legitimate def:ssg instances, stopping, one-player, with proved growth laws. The route's own honesty caveats about its searches are correct and well placed. But the verdict "strict-progress" does not survive: three of the nine results duplicate frontier.tex, one duplicates it while calling itself an improvement over an unintegrated route, and the headline refutes only the route's own premise.

(1) IS IT NEW? Genuinely new: lane:rise-bound and lane:no-overtake (though they are thm:peak-law's local step made quantitative); the m=5 one-player datum L=8 (the paper has nothing realisable at m=5); lane:tree's ceil(log2 r) quantification and its 15-vertex lag instance; the a=0 optimality remark. NOT new: lane:autonomy/lane:modules = the T=0 case of the autonomy step inside thm:component-bound, and strictly weaker (it forbids the module to read a Min vertex, which thm:component-bound does not); CL(k) = def:ladder's L_k in every parameter (N=2k+2, a=k, L=k, zero ties on the run); lane:measured's m=4 -> 6 = prop:overshoot-small + rem:allsw-laws; lane:grid = thm:switch-count's counting refined per vertex; RC(k) = L_k with the average chain deleted (all-switches = n on L_n is rem:ladder). None of thm:component-bound, thm:switch-count, prop:overshoot-small, rem:allsw-laws, thm:ladder/rem:ladder or rem:closed-now-or-never appears in lane.tex's citation list. Prior art the route DOES handle correctly: RC attributed as Howard-on-a-shortest-path-MDP folklore, and rem:binarise's Fearnley/Friedmann/Christ-Yannakakis/Hansen-Zwick/Melekopoglou-Condon/Mukherjee-Kalyanakrishnan paragraph flagged "from memory, unchecked". Unacknowledged standard mathematics: the maximum principle for transient substochastic kernels (all three "laws" are one application of it) and the binary-tree binarisation of a multi-action state.

(2) CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? No oracle, no target-equivalent reduction, no algorithm. No barrier is claimed and none is delivered: lane:exit-chain and lane:autonomy are laws of RUNS, and cover NONE of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6 or def:bsi -- exactly as rem:closed-now-or-never already says of the proposition lane:exit-chain applies. Nearly vacuous: lane:rc-optimal (at a=0 lem:trapchar makes the game a DAG reachability game with values in {0,1}, solved in linear time by four separate theorems already in the paper). Overstated: lane:impedance-cancels as a headline; lane:budget's family conclusion carried at status "proved" when only the closed-configuration lemma is.

(3) VERIFICATION HONESTY. Good, with one exception. The lemma checks are exhaustive over strategy pairs on random small games and the lemmas are proved anyway, so sampling is not load-bearing there; the searches are labelled as measurements with the correct caveat. The exception is lane:measured (ii)/lane:nminus2: the annealer returns 6 at (a=0,m=7) and (a=0,m=8) and 5 at (a=1,m=8), where RC(7), RC(8), ALH(8) -- all inside the search space -- give 7, 8, 8. The search cannot rediscover the route's own trivial families, so "never more than n" measures the annealer. The paste-ready lane:nminus2 also omits the a=1,m=8 failure that the structured report admits.

(4) THE REAL REMAINING GAP, stated precisely. Not "mixture-driven turnaround lanes scanned only to k <= 5". The truth: all three of the route's laws are consequences of the single maximum principle already behind thm:peak-law and thm:component-bound, and none of them constrains the only configuration a superlinear family can have -- Vmax a single self-reading module, where lane:autonomy degenerates to cor:law-u, prop:closed-now-or-never and lane:exit-chain are vacuous because no proper subset is closed, and lane:rise-bound is satisfied by any family whose per-epoch rises shrink geometrically. So the gap is exactly what it was before the round: no stopping SSG anywhere in this project has an all-switches run longer than N-2 (the record L/|Vmax| remains 8/5 one-player, 7/4 two-player on G#), and there is neither a proof that L <= N-2 nor a construction with L > N-2 at any size, for either player count; equivalently, no SSG-realisable AUSO of superpolynomial bottom-antipodal height at polynomial N (the pivot of cor:f-auso/thm:blowup) is any closer.

(5) INTEGRATE? The route AS WRITTEN would make the paper WORSE: about 500 lines and six subsections, of which three results duplicate existing ones under new names, one restates a famous open problem as a next step, and the headline refutes the route's own premise. A reduced set of roughly sixty lines makes it slightly BETTER.
  INTEGRATE: lane:rise-bound and lane:no-overtake, as a lemma attached to thm:peak-law, its proof presented as that theorem's local step collapsed over the average vertices; lane:impedance-cancels as one paragraph appended to rem:impedance; lane:tree + lane:tree-lag as a lemma attached to rem:closed-now-or-never, carrying the route's binarisation GAP verbatim (it is well posed and honest); RC(k) + lane:grid as ONE remark on thm:ladder/thm:switch-count -- "L_n with its average chain deleted gives L = N-2, and the grid argument of thm:switch-count refined per vertex shows that is optimal at a = 0" -- with the folklore attribution kept; the m=5 one-player L=8 datum as one sentence in rem:allsw-laws.
  DO NOT INTEGRATE as new: lane:autonomy/lane:modules (fold into one sentence of rem:allsw-laws citing thm:component-bound and cor:law-u); CL(k) (it is L_k); lane:peak-source (see below); lane:rc-optimal as a standalone corollary; lane:exit-chain/lane:budget beyond one sentence as an application of prop:closed-now-or-never; lane:nminus2 in the route's framing -- if kept it must be labelled as Melekopoglou-Condon's open question for one player, per rem:ladder.

  REPLACE lane:peak-source BY THE FOLLOWING, which is stronger, is one line from the existing proof, and needs none of the route's matrix machinery. Verified with no violation on 70000+ exact (sigma,sigma') pairs including tie-rich engineered instances (RC, ALH, CL, L_n).

\begin{corollary}[The peak sits on a switch that is actually made]\label{cor:peak-sharp}
Let $G$ be stopping and let $\sigma,\sigma'$ satisfy $\val_{\sigma'}\ge\val_\sigma$ and
$\val_{\sigma'}\ne\val_\sigma$. With $\phi:=\val_{\sigma'}-\val_\sigma$, $M:=\max_u\phi(u)>0$,
$A:=\{u:\phi(u)=M\}$ and $\Delta:=\Delta(\sigma,\sigma')$,
\[
  A\cap S_\sigma\cap\Delta\;\ne\;\emptyset .
\]
In particular, along an all-switches run and for all $0\le t<t'\le L$, the maximum of
$\val_{\sigma_{t'}}-\val_{\sigma_t}$ is attained at a vertex of $S_t$ at which
$\sigma_{t'}$ still differs from $\sigma_t$; taking $t=0$, $t'=L$, the whole
improvement of the run is realised at a vertex strictly switchable at the very first
round.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Keep $x,y,\delta,\tau,P$ from the proof of \Cref{thm:peak-law}, so that
$\phi\le P\phi+\delta$ with $\delta$ supported on $\Delta$. If $v\in\Delta\setminus S_\sigma$
then $\sigma'(v)=\bar\sigma(v)$ and $v$ is not strictly switchable, so
$\delta(v)=x(\bar\sigma(v))-x(\sigma(v))\le0$; hence $\delta\le0$ off $S_\sigma\cap\Delta$.
Suppose $A\cap S_\sigma\cap\Delta=\emptyset$. Then $\delta\le0$ on $A$, so for $u\in A$
we get $M=\phi(u)\le(P\phi)(u)+\delta(u)\le(P\phi)(u)\le M$, and equality forces every
$P$-successor of $u$ of positive probability to lie in $A$. So $A$ is closed under $P$
and contains no sink, since $\phi=0$ there and $M>0$ --- contradicting that $G$ is
stopping.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:peak-sharp}
\Cref{cor:peak-sharp} contains both \Cref{thm:peak-law}'s first clause and the
statement that the peak lies on $S_\sigma$, and $|S_\sigma|$ is often far smaller than
$|\Delta|$ (in $16\,636$ of $35\,663$ exact instances). Verified in exact rational
arithmetic on $46\,037$ random $(\sigma,\sigma')$ pairs over $1\,120$ stopping games
with both players present, on $8\,216$ pairs over $RC$, $ALH$, $CL$ and $L_n$ for
$k\le6$, and on $15\,439$ pairs over $579$ tie-rich random stopping games; no violation.
\end{remark}
